subject.title: [Feature]: only accept signed messages to prevent prompt injection [improvement] [hardening]

question: Should owner-key signed inbound-message verification be handled as a channel/plugin verifier using existing hooks, require a new generic pre-routing SDK/security capability, or be rejected as overlapping the current pairing/allowlist model?
rationale: The request changes the inbound trust boundary and would define key registration, rejection logging, per-channel policy, and whether the open pre-routing hook work is required before implementation.

options.title: Plugin-owned verifier first
options.body: Keep core lean by documenting or building a channel/email plugin pattern for signature checks, then extend SDK only for a proven missing pre-routing suppression seam.

options.title: Generic SDK auth gate
options.body: Design a typed pre-agent verification capability with key storage, audit logging, fail-open/fail-closed semantics, and upgrade behavior before any implementation.

options.title: Decline core signatures
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers decide pairing, allowlists, platform auth, and tool policy are the intended model for this threat.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned verifier first
recommendation.body: Keep core lean by documenting or building a channel/email plugin pattern for signature checks, then extend SDK only for a proven missing pre-routing suppression seam.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/security boundary choice and he has the strongest documented project decision and recent security-doc provenance.
